subject: Westus5 node recycle & safety window - customer notice and ops plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Price <danielle.price@helix-analytics.com>, support@helix-analytics.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Westus5 node recycle & safety window - customer notice and ops plan

Hello Danielle / Helix team,

Heads-up that we have a scheduled, low-risk maintenance window for the westus5 inference pool on Friday, Nov 19 between 02:00 - 06:00 PT (09:00 - 13:00 UTC). The work is a staged node recycle + driver micro-upgrade to address an IO degradation we've observed at low frequency in a small subset of hosts.

What to expect for your workloads:
- We will perform rolling node recycles across the pool so no full-region outage is expected.
- During a recycle for a host that currently has live inference traffic, you may see short-lived connection refreshes and a micro-latency spike (typical < 300ms extra per token) for in-flight requests as sessions are migrated.
- We limit concurrency to keep the active capacity impact to under ~3% of your provisioned capacity at any minute.
- Long-running KV sessions will be preserved where possible; however, if your workload relies on pinned local caches, expect a warm-up after failover.

Recommended customer actions (optional):
1) If you have pinned model instances, consider enabling our fallback routing to a compatible variant for the 4-hour window.
2) For critical latency SLOs, schedule non-critical batch jobs outside the window.
3) If you have a sustained in-memory KV dependency, let us know so we can schedule a minor DNS affinity to minimize evictions.

Attachments: westus5-safecycle-maintenance-plan.pdf (detailed timeline), canary-checklist.md (internal runbook).

If there are any constraints for Helix (e.g., blackout windows, active launches), reply to this thread and we will coordinate. Otherwise we will proceed with the plan and post a summary after completion.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

--
Note: For additional context see the ops page: https://redwood.example.com/ops/incidents/WUS5-20261111

Grace / Jordan — looping you in on Helix response. They want confirmation on logs retention and whether fallback affects billing. Please action:

- Grace: confirm retention window for eviction/audit logs and include link to the S3 bucket/retention policy.
- Jordan: coordinate with Billing to confirm if routing to variant model during a fallback is billed at the consistent per-token rate or if proxies are charged differently. Also add a note about how we'll annotate the usage so Helix can reconcile with their finance team.

Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Westus5 node recycle & safety window - customer notice and ops plan

Hi Danielle — quick follow-up with answers from our side: 

1) Logs & retention: eviction/hand-off audit events and the per-request trace will be retained for 30 days in the customer audit bucket. You can access them via the audit link we shared (we will grant a read-only token for the maintenance window).
2) Billing: fallback routing to a compatible model variant is billed at the standard per-token rate for the model that handles the request; there is no additional proxy surcharge. We will annotate the usage with an "maintenance_routing" tag so you can filter these tokens in your billing exports.

Plan still on for Fri Nov 19 02:00 - 06:00 PT. We will run the internal canary at 01:30 PT and hold for 30 mins before proceeding. If anything unexpected shows up during canary, we will abort and reschedule.

If you'd like a short 15-minute call to walk through the recovery/rollback steps, we can do that tomorrow morning PT.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
